posts.title: How I Use AI in Web Development — and Where I Don't
posts.description: A practical look at my AI-assisted workflow: where Claude, Claude Code and ChatGPT speed up the work, and where human review stays non-negotiable.
posts.tags:
AI-assisted development
Claude Code
Next.js
Workflow
posts.content:
"Do you use AI to build websites?" is one of the first questions clients ask me now. The short answer is yes — every day. The more useful answer is *how*, because the way a developer uses AI decides whether you get a faster project or a fragile one.

Since June 2023 I've been building, migrating and maintaining client websites at Krushna53 with Next.js, React, Sanity CMS and WordPress. Over that time AI tools moved from "interesting" to a normal part of my workflow. Here's exactly where they help, and where I deliberately keep the work in my own hands.

## The tools I actually use

- **Claude** — thinking through requirements, planning features and explaining unfamiliar code.
- **Claude Code** — working directly inside a codebase: building features, creating components, debugging.
- **ChatGPT** — quick questions and second opinions.
- **MCP** — connecting AI tools to the services and data a project already uses.
- **Cursor** — AI help while editing code.

None of these replace the project. They speed up specific steps inside it.

## Where AI speeds things up

### 1. Understanding requirements and planning

Before writing code, I use AI to break a brief or a Figma design into pages, components and content types, and to spot questions I need to ask the client early. A clearer plan at the start means fewer surprises later.

### 2. Building components and repetitive code

A lot of web development is repetitive: similar React components, form handling, layout variations, TypeScript types. AI is very good at producing a solid first version of this kind of code, so I can spend my time on the parts that are specific to your project.

### 3. Working inside existing codebases

Many projects aren't new — they're an existing site that needs a feature, a fix or a cleanup. Claude Code helps me understand how an unfamiliar codebase is organised, find where a change belongs and trace bugs faster.

### 4. CMS and migration work

Setting up Sanity CMS schemas, modelling content, connecting APIs and moving content from WordPress all involve a lot of careful but repetitive steps. AI helps me move through them faster.

![Sanity Studio with a blog post imported from WordPress, showing its slug, old URL redirect and SEO fields](@media:blog/how-i-use-ai-in-web-development/sanity-studio "Example: a post migrated from WordPress into Sanity Studio, with its old URL kept as a 301 redirect")

## Where I don't rely on AI

This is the part that matters most for you as a client.

- **Reviewing the code.** Every piece of AI-generated code is read and understood before it goes into your project. If I can't explain why it works, it doesn't ship.
- **Debugging and verifying.** AI can suggest a fix; I confirm the real cause and check that the fix doesn't break something else.
- **Testing the result.** I test the finished site across browsers and devices myself — layouts, forms, content editing and performance.
- **Choosing the right tool.** Whether your project needs Next.js, Sanity or WordPress is a decision based on your requirements, your team and your budget — not on what's trendy or what an AI suggests by default.

AI-generated code can look correct and still miss an edge case, a design detail or the way your content is actually structured. That's exactly why review and testing stay in my hands.

> AI accelerates the process. Engineering judgment ensures the quality.

## What my process looks like

1. **Understand requirements** — your goals, design, current website and content.
2. **Plan** — technology, structure, timeline and estimate.
3. **AI-assisted development** — building faster with the tools above.
4. **Human code review** — every change checked by me.
5. **Testing** — responsive layouts, functionality and fixes.
6. **Deployment** — launch, with preview links shared along the way.

## What this means for your project

- **Less time spent on the repetitive parts**, so more attention goes to the parts that make your site work for your business.
- **Regular progress updates and preview links**, so you see the work as it develops.
- **Code that a person has read, understood and tested** — not something generated and shipped blind.

If you're planning a new website, a WordPress to Next.js migration or AI features for an existing site, I'm happy to walk you through how this workflow would apply to your project. [Tell me about your project](/contact) and I'll reply with a practical approach, timeline and estimate.

posts.title: What It Really Takes to Add an AI Chatbot to Your Website
posts.description: Learn what business owners need to prepare, how the build process works, and what shapes the technical scope when adding an AI chatbot to your website.
posts.tags:
AI Chatbot
AI Integration
Next.js
Web Development

coverScene.labels:
What services do you offer for websites?
I build Next.js websites and integrate AI APIs into applications.

posts.content:
Adding an AI feature to a business website often sounds complex. Many founders and marketing managers want a site assistant to answer customer questions, direct visitors, or assist with sales inquiries, but they are unsure where to begin or what technical steps are required.

Building a useful AI chatbot is not just about placing a widget on a page. It requires clean technical integration, clear source business information, and careful human review to ensure every response is accurate and reliable for your visitors.

## What an AI chatbot can handle on your website

Many business owners assume an AI chatbot is either a basic decision-tree widget or a complex system that replaces human support entirely. In reality, a custom AI chatbot serves as a context-aware assistant tailored to your specific business content.

Unlike traditional live chat systems that rely on scripted decision trees, an AI chatbot powered by modern AI APIs reads user prompts and formulates answers based on the knowledge base you provide. This allows it to handle routine customer questions effectively.

- **Answering service queries:** Explaining your core services, capabilities, and delivery models based on your official documentation.
- **Guiding visitors:** Helping prospective clients navigate to the right contact form, product category, or portfolio showcase.
- **Gathering preliminary details:** Collecting key project requirements from visitors before handing the conversation off to a team member.
- **Providing round-the-clock information:** Delivering immediate answers to common questions when your team is offline.

If you want to explore what intelligent features fit your application, you can check my [AI Integration & Development service](/services#service-1) details for more examples.

## What you need to prepare before development begins

Before any code is written or APIs are connected, the single most important element of an AI chatbot is the quality of the information you provide. The chatbot can only be as accurate as the underlying business documentation it references.

When I start an AI integration project, I work with clients to collect structured data. If your site content is scattered or out of date, the AI tool may produce inaccurate answers.

Here is a practical breakdown of the material you should gather before initiating a chatbot build:

- **Service descriptions:** Comprehensive overviews of what you offer, target clients, and deliverable structures.
- **Frequently asked questions:** Real questions past customers have asked, along with verified answers.
- **Brand voice guidelines:** Instructions on tone, formatting preference, and topics the chatbot should avoid.
- **Escalation rules:** Direct instructions on when and how the assistant should prompt the user to fill out a contact form or send an email.

```visual
{"kind":"checklist","title":"Preparation Checklist for AI Chatbot Projects","items":["Organized product and service documentation","Verified list of FAQs and answers","Brand tone and voice guidelines","Clear boundaries on off-topic questions","Contact form and lead handoff rules","Access to existing site codebase or API access"]}
```

## How the technical build process works

When building web applications, I follow a structured approach to ensure the interface is responsive and the backend integration remains stable.

I build custom frontends using modern frameworks like Next.js and React. This ensures the chat widget fits seamlessly into your brand design without slowing down your site layout. For the backend logic, I connect your application to suitable AI models using modern APIs like the Claude API.

In my own development workflow, I use tools like Claude Code and Cursor to build components and speed up routine coding tasks. However, engineering judgment remains key. Every piece of AI logic and code is manually reviewed and tested by me before deployment. You can read more about this balance in my article on [how I use AI in web development](/blog/how-i-use-ai-in-web-development).

### The standard build workflow

1. **Data structuring:** Cleaning and organizing your documentation into clear context prompts.
2. **UI component development:** Building custom React components for the chat box, chat bubble, and message stream.
3. **API integration:** Connecting the frontend to secure API routes to pass user prompts to the AI model.
4. **Context handling:** Ensuring the AI assistant stays on topic and references your business information.

```visual
{"kind":"steps","title":"The Step-by-Step AI Chatbot Build Workflow","steps":[{"title":"Structure context data","text":"Organize your business documentation, service guidelines, and FAQs into structured prompt context."},{"title":"Build user interface","text":"Develop responsive Next.js and React components for the chat window and message streams."},{"title":"Connect AI APIs","text":"Integrate secure API handlers to communicate directly with backend AI model endpoints."},{"title":"Review and test","text":"Test responses manually across devices to verify layout stability, speed, and output accuracy."}]}
```

## What affects project complexity and technical scope

Not all AI chatbot implementations require the same level of effort. Understanding what factors increase complexity helps you plan your project goals effectively.

- **Static context vs. dynamic data:** A chatbot that answers questions based on a fixed document is straightforward to build. If your chatbot needs to pull live inventory levels, pricing tables, or user account details from an external database, additional API endpoints and integration steps are required.
- **Interface customizability:** Adding a basic floating chat widget takes less development effort than building a full-screen, custom-themed interactive assistant embedded directly within custom dashboard pages.
- **Tech stack integration:** If your website is built on custom [Next.js & React Development](/services#service-3) architecture, adding custom server routes is very clean. Integrating AI capabilities into legacy systems may require additional configuration.
- **Fallback and handoff handling:** Setting up graceful fallbacks—such as automatically capturing lead information when the chatbot encounters an unknown question—requires dedicated UI flows and form endpoints.

## Ensuring quality, security, and human review

One of the biggest concerns business owners have is the risk of an AI chatbot generating incorrect information or off-brand responses. Preventing this requires strict prompt design and thorough edge-case testing.

During development, I establish explicit instructions within the chatbot prompt architecture. These rules direct the model to admit when it does not possess specific information, rather than inventing answers. I also ensure that API keys and sensitive credentials remain secure on server-side environments, preventing public exposure.

Finally, careful manual testing across mobile screens, tablets, and desktop browsers ensures the chat window opens smoothly, renders Markdown text correctly, and provides a pleasant user experience for your site visitors.

Adding an AI chatbot to your website is a practical way to provide instant answers to visitors and streamline incoming inquiries. By pairing clear business documentation with modern AI APIs and clean Next.js architecture, you can give your website a powerful interactive feature.

If you are planning to integrate AI capabilities into your existing website or build a new application, I can help you plan and execute the project. [Tell me about your project](/contact) to discuss your goals, technical requirements, and timeline.

posts.content:
Many business owners feel strong pressure to add artificial intelligence to their websites. With headlines constantly promoting new software, it is easy to assume your site needs an AI feature to remain relevant. However, adding interactive tools just to look modern often leads to bloated code, higher monthly software costs, and frustrated users who simply want to find basic information.

As a developer who builds digital products with Next.js, React, and Sanity CMS, I focus on practical web software that solves concrete problems. You do not need complex gimmicks to benefit from modern AI APIs. Here are five practical AI features that provide immediate value to your website visitors, along with guidance on what you should avoid.

## Intelligent site search that understands user intent

Traditional website search relies heavily on exact keyword matching. If a visitor types "affordable software consultation" but your service page uses the heading "budget-friendly application strategy," standard search components often return zero results. This disconnect forces potential clients to navigate your menu manually or leave your website entirely.

Semantic search uses modern AI APIs to read the intent behind a query rather than matching literal letters. When a user enters a phrase in natural language, the system evaluates the underlying concept and retrieves the most relevant pages, products, or documentation.

This feature suits websites with large product catalogs, extensive documentation, or deep resource libraries. By implementing custom search through my [AI Integration & Development](/services#service-1) service, you help visitors get answers quickly while keeping your database structure clean. It turns complex site navigation into a simple experience.

## Context-aware Q&A trained on your actual content

Static FAQ pages often fail to answer specific customer questions. Visitors have to scroll through long lists of generic questions, hoping to spot a sentence that applies to their situation. A context-aware Q&A feature replaces that static experience with a flexible input box.

Unlike generic public AI models that pull answers from the broader internet, a context-aware system operates strictly on your approved knowledge base. It scans your existing website copy, service documents, or product guides to synthesize a direct answer. If the information does not exist in your reference files, the system clearly states that it does not know, rather than making up facts.

This setup is ideal for service providers, software platforms, and agencies that spend significant time answering repetitive inquiries. You can review my guide on [what it really takes to add an AI chatbot](/blog/what-it-really-takes-to-add-an-ai-chatbot) to understand the technical structure required for this feature.

```visual
{"kind":"steps","title":"How Context-Aware Q&A Operates","steps":[{"title":"Visitor asks question","text":"A user types a specific question about your services into the website query bar."},{"title":"System scans context","text":"The application searches your stored website pages and verified documentation files."},{"title":"Answer is generated","text":"The AI builds a clear answer using only your approved business information."},{"title":"Sources are cited","text":"The visitor sees the direct answer alongside links to full site documentation."}]}
```

## Smart forms and automated lead classification

Form friction is one of the main reasons potential clients leave a website before reaching out. Long forms with rigid input requirements create frustration, especially on mobile devices. Smart forms use background processing to assist visitors as they complete your inquiry form.

As users type their project description or request details, an integrated AI model can automatically suggest appropriate categories, validate technical details, or clean up formatted entries. This reduces the number of steps a user must complete manually while keeping the incoming data structured for your team.

Behind the scenes, the system can evaluate incoming messages and route them automatically. For example, urgent support requests can be tagged and forwarded to technical personnel, while high-intent project inquiries go straight to your sales inbox. This setup improves internal response times without adding work for your team.

## Internal CMS content assistants for your team

Not every useful AI feature needs to be visible to your website visitors. In fact, some of the most effective implementations operate inside your content management system to assist your marketing team.

When I build custom content platforms using [Figma to Next.js + Sanity CMS](/services#service-4), I can integrate dedicated writing assistants inside Sanity Studio. Your team can use these tools to draft blog post outlines, reformat raw notes into structured sections, generate SEO metadata, or create product descriptions directly inside the editing panel.

Because these tools operate strictly within your internal workflow, you retain complete editorial control. No text reaches your live website until a human editor reviews, refines, and approves the content. This keeps your published writing accurate and consistent with your brand tone.

## Dynamic page summaries for quick scanning

Online readers rarely read long articles or detailed service offerings line by line. Instead, most visitors scan headers, bullet points, and callout boxes to decide whether the page contains the information they need.

Dynamic summary blocks sit near the top of long-form pages, offering a concise overview of the key points covered below. Using background API routes, the system reads your main body content and extracts three to four distinct key takeaways.

This feature works exceptionally well for technical blogs, comprehensive service breakdowns, and multi-page guides. It allows busy readers to digest core concepts instantly, while keeping the full detailed text available for visitors who want a deeper breakdown.

## AI features small businesses should skip

While practical AI integrations improve user experience, adding features without a clear purpose can harm your business brand. Some popular AI tools sound impressive in marketing materials but deliver poor results in real-world usage.

You should avoid unrestricted public chatbots that draw answers from general internet training data. These bots frequently share incorrect information, misquote pricing, or promise services you do not offer. You should also avoid automated blog publishing systems that generate and publish articles without human oversight. Search engines penalize low-quality, fully automated content, and visitors quickly spot unrefined text.

Finally, skip complex voice widgets and 3D animated avatars. Most web users prefer reading clear text and clicking straightforward buttons over speaking into their browser microphone or watching virtual characters load.

```visual
{"kind":"compare","title":"Evaluating AI Features for Your Website","left":{"label":"Features to Adopt","points":["Intent-based semantic search","Grounded content Q&A tools","Smart form validation","Internal CMS draft helpers","Concise page takeaway blocks"]},"right":{"label":"Features to Skip","points":["Unrestricted public bots","Automated unreviewed blog publishing","Complex web voice widgets","Animated 3D digital avatars","Distracting auto popups"]}}
```

## How to choose the right implementation strategy

Adding AI to your website should always serve a practical business objective, such as reducing repetitive support questions, capturing better contact leads, or helping visitors find products faster. Starting with a clear technical scope ensures you spend resources on features that deliver measurable utility.

When planning an implementation, your site structure and platform matter. Modern frameworks like Next.js handle API integrations efficiently on the server side, keeping API keys secure and page load speeds fast. If you want to see how I combine modern coding practices with artificial intelligence tools during development, read my breakdown on [How I Use AI in Web Development](/blog/how-i-use-ai-in-web-development).

Focus on simple, context-aware tools that support your existing website content. A well-designed search input or a smart contact form will always provide more value than a flashy gimmick.

Building useful AI features requires a balance between modern technology and clean engineering. If you are considering adding intelligent search, content Q&A, or smart forms to your website, I can help you select and build the right solution.

[Contact me](/contact) to discuss your project requirements, receive a clear breakdown of technical options, and get an estimate for your website.
